payload.prompt: Erstellen und senden Sie eine Rechnung an den Kunden Flussgold GmbH (Org.-Nr. 965203516) über 19650 NOK ohne MwSt. Die Rechnung betrifft Cloud-Speicher.

payload.goal: Erstelle und sende eine Rechnung an Flussgold GmbH (Org.-Nr. 965203516) über 19650 NOK ohne MwSt. für Cloud-Speicher.
success_checks: Kunde Flussgold GmbH mit Org.-Nr. 965203516 ist im System vorhanden
Rechnung über 19650 NOK (exkl. MwSt., 0%) für Cloud-Speicher wurde erstellt
Rechnung wurde erfolgreich an den Kunden gesendet
risk_notes: Sandbox ist leer – Kunde Flussgold GmbH muss zuerst angelegt werden
Kein Bankkonto konfiguriert – muss vor Rechnungserstellung eingerichtet werden
Keine E-Mail-Adresse für Flussgold GmbH angegeben – Versand per E-Mail nicht möglich ohne diese Information
Kein Produktdatensatz für 'Cloud-Speicher' vorhanden – muss ggf. angelegt werden
MwSt. explizit als 0% (ohne MwSt.) angegeben – VAT-Exempt muss korrekt konfiguriert sein
Währung NOK angenommen – Systemwährung muss übereinstimmen
payload.suggested_first_action: Bankkonto einrichten (POST /bank/account), dann Kunden Flussgold GmbH anlegen (POST /customer)
ordered_steps: 2. Kunden anlegen: POST /customer mit name='Flussgold GmbH', organizationNumber='965203516'
3. Produkt anlegen: POST /product mit name='Cloud-Speicher', vatType=EXEMPT (0%)
4. Auftrag erstellen: POST /order mit customerId=<id> und currency='NOK'
5. Auftragszeile hinzufügen: POST /order/orderline mit productId=<id>, quantity=1, unitPriceExcludingVat=19650, vatPercent=0
6. Rechnung erstellen: PUT /order/{id}/invoice (Rechnung aus Auftrag generieren)
7. Rechnung senden: PUT /invoice/{id}/:send (Versand per E-Mail oder Post)

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Send invoice by ID and sendType. Optionally override email recipient.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.
Add new timesheet entry. Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination is supported.

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Use query parameter sendType=EMAIL.
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedPrice=<amount> (camelCase).
If name already exists (422 'Navnet er i bruk'), use GET /activity?name=... and reuse.
For project activities, set activityType='PROJECT_GENERAL_ACTIVITY'.
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.
Requires project, activity, employee, date, hours.
Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination.
hours is a decimal number (e.g. 8.0, 7.5).

payload.trace_example_task: Invoice with milestone/project. 9 API calls, 1 recoverable error.

payload.text:
Let me analyze the task:

1. Create and send an invoice to customer Flussgold GmbH (Org.-Nr. 965203516)
2. Amount: 19650 NOK excluding VAT (0% VAT = exempt)
3. For: Cloud-Speicher (Cloud Storage)
4. Send the invoice

The sandbox_discovery shows the customer already exists with id 108251047.

Steps:
1. GET /ledger/account?number=1920 (bank account setup)
2. PUT /ledger/account/{id} to configure bank account
3. Customer already exists (id: 108251047) - skip creation


4. Create order with customer reference, then add an order line for Cloud-Speicher at 19650 NOK with 0% VAT, generate the invoice from that order, and send it out.

Let me start by fetching the bank account details so I have what I need for the PUT request.

payload.headline: Agent crashed mid-execution due to disk space error, leaving invoice incomplete/unsent
what_went_wrong: Fatal [Errno 28] No space left on device error halted execution after planning, preventing most API calls from completing.
Checks 3, 4, 5 failed — likely order line creation, invoice generation, or invoice sending steps were never executed due to the crash.
Agent had no recovery mechanism after the disk error; execution jumped directly to scoring with partial results.
Only 4/7 checks passed, suggesting basic customer/order creation succeeded but invoice finalization and sending did not.
what_worked: Customer lookup and basic order creation appear to have partially succeeded (checks 1, 2, 6, 7 passed).
Planner correctly identified the task steps and recognized the customer already existed (id: 108251047).
what_to_try_next: Ensure sufficient disk space on the agent host before running; implement a pre-flight disk space check to fail fast with a clear error.
Add checkpoint/resume logic so that if a crash occurs mid-run, completed steps (customer found, order created) are not repeated and remaining steps can continue.
Re-run the task: the customer exists, so skip creation, create order + orderline (19650 NOK, 0% VAT, Cloud-Speicher), then PUT /order/{id}/invoice and POST to send it.
